payload.rebuttal: fixed: The subset-capability probe in run_witness no longer uses declared[0].witness. It now requires the caller to pass the plain (no-subset) `tests` GateResult, and draws the probe id from that result's own `collected` list — a name genuinely known to exist, never a criterion's operator-written `witness` field. A stale or renamed witness id in one criterion can therefore no longer be mistaken, before witness_gate is ever invoked, for 'this repo's `tests` gate cannot be filtered by subset at all': the probe now succeeds whenever the repo genuinely supports subset filtering, regardless of what any individual criterion declares, so it stops discarding every criterion's chance at a real finding on the strength of one bad id. If no readable enumeration exists to draw a canary from, `witness` now reports `skip` for that honest reason ('no readable test enumeration to probe subset support with') rather than guessing. run_suite was updated to locate and pass the plain `tests` result through. Added tests/test_gates.py::test_a_stale_witness_id_does_not_trigger_a_false_skip, which reproduces exactly the scenario the critic described (a single criterion whose witness id no longer exists, against a `tests` gate that answers a real, collected id just fine) and asserts the old bug's outcome (`skip`, discarding everything without ever really trying) no longer occurs — witness_gate now genuinely runs and the criterion's own bad id surfaces as `error` from inside it, which is witness_gate's own documented (and out-of-scope-to-change) behavior for a `tests` gate result it cannot read, not a premature blanket `skip`. I did not claim this also fixes witness_gate's separate, explicitly-out-of-scope 'a later criterion's real error discards an earlier criterion's real survivor' behavior (consequence #1 from the spec) — that lives inside saffron/gates/core/witness.py, which is forbidden to this spec, and the spec itself says that is not this spec's to fix. The two are different bugs at different layers: the one the critic flagged was in the wiring's own pre-loop probe, and that one is fixed.
